packages.label: רְדִיפָה וְקֵרוּב לַה'
packages.label_en: Persecution and Drawing Close to Hashem
packages.reason: These concepts share the essential nature of the paradoxical dynamic the Rebbe describes: opposition and pursuit are in truth the mechanism of drawing near to Hashem. They are all expressions of the same inverted reality — what appears as an act of driving away is in fact an act of bringing close. The Rebbe states explicitly: 'וְכָל מַה שֶּׁחוֹלְקִין עָלָיו יוֹתֵר, מְקָרְבִין אוֹתוֹ יוֹתֵר לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ'. He then gives the bechina name for this entire dynamic: 'וְזֶה בְּחִינַת: וּפַרְעֹה הִקְרִיב' — Pharaoh's pursuit IS the archetypal bechina of this dynamic. The bechina chain is: חֲלוֹקָה (opposition) = רְדִיפָה (pursuit) = in truth קֵרוּב (drawing close). These are not sequential cause-and-effect but three faces of the same inverted reality: the act of opposition IS the act of drawing close, as mediated by the person's flight. The dominant node is בְּרִיחָה לַה' (fleeing to Hashem) because the Rebbe places it at the center of the dynamic — it is the pivotal act that transforms persecution into closeness.

merge_notes.reason: The Rebbe opens by equating these two: 'כְּשֶׁחוֹלְקִין עַל הָאָדָם, נִמְצָא שֶׁרוֹדְפִין אוֹתוֹ'. Being opposed (machloket/cholek) = being pursued (rodef). They are two expressions of the same hostile action from the outside. Shared nature: the external force that drives a person away.

The Rebbe equates these directly: fleeing to Hashem in every place IS being drawn closer to Hashem. 'נִמְצָא שֶׁבְּכָל מָקוֹם בּוֹרֵחַ לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ' = 'מְקָרְבִין אוֹתוֹ יוֹתֵר לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ'. The flight and the closeness are two descriptions of the same act — fleeing to Hashem IS drawing close to Hashem. Shared nature: the person's turning toward God under pressure.

The Rebbe explicitly states: 'וְזֶה בְּחִינַת: וּפַרְעֹה הִקְרִיב — שֶׁהִקְרִיב אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל לַאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם, שֶׁעַל־יְדֵי רְדִיפָתוֹ אוֹתָם נִתְקָרְבוּ יוֹתֵר לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ'. Pharaoh's act of pursuit (his רְדִיפָה) IS the bechina of ופרעה הקריב — 'the one who brings near'. The persecutor and the bringer-near are the same person expressing the same bechina from two directions. Shared nature: the external hostile force that is in truth the agent of drawing near.

packages.label: הַשֵּׁם בְּכָל מָקוֹם
packages.reason: These concepts share the essential nature of divine omnipresence — the principle that there is no place devoid of Hashem, whether the heights of heaven or the depths of the grave. This is the theological foundation that makes the entire dynamic of Package 1 possible: the person can always flee to Hashem in every place precisely because Hashem is in every place. The Rebbe states this explicitly as the bechina of Psalm 139:8: 'הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּכָל מָקוֹם, בִּבְחִינַת (תהילים קל״ט:ח׳): אִם אֶסַּק שָׁמַיִם שָׁם אָתָּה, וְאַצִּיעָה שְׁאוֹל הִנֶּךָּ'. The concept of omnipresence and the Psalm verse are two expressions of the same reality: the inescapable divine presence that fills all space. The שָׁמַיִם (heaven) and שְׁאוֹל (the grave/depths) serve as extreme poles to express the totality of this presence — they are bechina instances of the full span of divine presence.

merge_notes.reason: The Rebbe explicitly calls the Psalm verse the bechina of divine omnipresence: 'הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּכָל מָקוֹם, בִּבְחִינַת... אִם אֶסַּק שָׁמַיִם שָׁם אָתָּה'. The two halves of the verse (heaven / grave) are not separate concepts but expressions of the single idea of total divine presence — from the highest extreme to the lowest. All three share the same essential nature: the totality of Hashem's presence that leaves no space unfilled.

Torah LM2/13 is the shortest Torah analyzed so far — two dense paragraphs built around a single paradox. Package 2 (omnipresence) provides the theological foundation (eitza) for Package 1 (pursuit → flight → closeness). The Torah's structure: Pkg2 (Hashem is everywhere) → [enables] → Pkg1 (persecution becomes closeness).

good_evil_mirror.analysis: Torah LM2/13 has no evil package. The Torah's structure is unusual: it reframes the evil (persecution, Pharaoh) as itself a good instrument — Pharaoh's pursuit IS the drawing-near. The 'evil' element (opponent/persecutor) is subsumed into the good package as an inverted expression of closeness. There is no independent evil cluster because the teaching's entire point is that opposition has no independent reality of its own — it is always, in truth, an act of bringing close. The evil is absorbed into the good dynamic.
good_evil_mirror.note: The חֲלוֹקָה (opposition) and פַּרְעֹה (archetypal persecutor) appear in Package 1 (good polarity) precisely because the Torah reframes them as instruments of closeness, not as an independent evil domain.
